prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1322; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle that entered on a red signal. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness following the impact and was seen at an urgent care facility the same day. No attorney representation noted at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes whiplash symptoms including limited neck rotation, headaches, and pain radiating into the upper shoulder. Claimant states they were wearing a seatbelt and that airbags did not deploy. Explained the claims process and the option to submit medical records directly. Claimant has not retained counsel and says they plan to handle the claim personally for now.

Entry 3: Received urgent care records and imaging order. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain consistent with whiplash injury. Physical therapy referral noted. Requested authorization for a rehabilitation evaluation and reviewed the treating provider's notes for consistency with the reported mechanism of injury. Third-party carrier has acknowledged liability for the collision but has not yet made a settlement offer.

Entry 4: Followed up with claimant regarding attendance at physical therapy sessions. Claimant reports missing one appointment due to work conflict and has rescheduled. Reminded claimant to keep all treatment records and receipts for out-of-pocket expenses such as prescriptions and transportation. Claimant asked about the timeline for resolution; explained that the timeline depends on treatment completion and medical documentation.

Entry 5: Reviewed updated physical therapy progress notes showing improved range of motion and decreasing pain levels. Claimant still reports intermittent headaches. Prepared a written summary of the injury documentation and sent a settlement evaluation request to the claims supervisor for review. Scheduled a call with claimant to explain the evaluation process and confirm contact information and preferred communication method.
